lyrics:
[Intro: bright piano chords, finger snaps]

[Verse 1: female voice, easy and warm]
First time around I ran every light
Ring by the spring, baby by July
Thought love was a train you catch at a run
Missed a lot of scenery. Wasn't much fun.

[Pre-Chorus: male voice, gentle]
So if I'm slow to hold your hand in town
It ain't doubt, girl. I'm just looking around.

[Chorus: both voices, claps and a light beat]
There's no hurry on a sure thing
No clock on a good night
We can take the long road, the slow dance, the porch side
If it's real today, it's real in the spring
No hurry on a sure thing

[Verse 2: male voice]
Your kids are still deciding if they like my jokes
My dog's already yours, he's the easiest of folks
We both got a drawer full of used-to-be
You don't have to empty yours to make room for me

[Pre-Chorus: female voice]
So if I don't say the big word yet
It's coming. It's just not out of breath.

[Chorus: both voices, claps and a light beat]
There's no hurry on a sure thing
No clock on a good night
We can take the long road, the slow dance, the porch side
If it's real today, it's real in the spring
No hurry on a sure thing

[Bridge: piano only, voices trading lines]
Twenty-five was all gas
Forty-five's got brakes
And a much better view of what it takes

[Final Chorus: fullest, harmonies stacked]
There's no hurry on a sure thing
No clock on a good night
We can take the long road, the slow dance, the porch side
If it's real today, it's real in the spring
No hurry on a sure thing

[Outro: piano, spoken, smiling]
No hurry.
None.
Okay. A little.
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 77 BPM, 4/4, B-flat major. Relaxed and bright, a slow head-nod.

VOICE: A duet. Female voice leads: warm, slightly husky, conversational. Male voice: soft country tenor with a little drawl. They trade verses and pre-choruses and sing the choruses in harmony. Three spoken words at the end.

INSTRUMENTS: Bright piano chords, finger snaps and handclaps, a light programmed beat with a soft kick, acoustic guitar, a warm bass, a little slide guitar answering in the choruses.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro piano. 0:10 Verse 1, her. 0:35 Pre-chorus, him. 0:47 Chorus 1. 1:12 Verse 2, him. 1:37 Pre-chorus, her. 1:49 Chorus 2. 2:14 Bridge, piano only. 2:32 Final chorus. 2:58 Outro, three spoken lines, ends 3:12.

PRODUCTION & MIX: 2017 pop-country crossover: clean, glossy, vocals forward, low end soft and round.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'Forty-five's got brakes' in the bridge at 2:20.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original calms a young couple who do not know where it is going. These two know exactly how it can go wrong, and choose slowness as a pleasure.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Wary, reassured, amused, quietly sure.
